solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Thin argument behind rushed revolution

indicators.note: a revolution turns something right round, so the word before it is read from the other end
behind places the quarrel word after the other piece rather than before it

blocks.note: rushed means ran, past tense
a row is a quarrel

explanation.surface: A feeble case made after a hurried uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind' puts the argument after the turned-round word, so the order is the reverse of the clue's.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrow and thin are synonyms for something of little width.

clue.text: Nab dossier that's found in beauty parlour

blocks.note: to nail a suspect is to catch them
a dossier is a file of documents

explanation.surface: Police seize incriminating papers discovered in a beauty salon.
explanation.definitionFit: A nail file is a manicure tool, an item any beauty salon keeps.

clue.text: Funds religious education courses abroad

indicators.note: abroad can mean widely scattered, so the letters before it are spread into a new order

blocks.note: RE is the school subject Religious Education
taken as written

explanation.surface: Money for theology classes held overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: Resources are a supply of money or assets, so funds is a synonym.

clue.text: Love singer Alfie accompanying woodwind instrument

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O
Alfie Boe is an English tenor

explanation.surface: A tenor sings a love song with woodwind backing.
explanation.definitionFit: The oboe is a double-reed member of the woodwind family.

clue.text: In fear about sons getting justice

indicators.note: about can mean all around or astir, so these letters get moved round into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
S is the abbreviation for son, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Frightened parents worried about their boys being treated justly in court.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairness is the quality of treating people justly, a near synonym of justice.

clue.text: Hope morning session upset no-one?

indicators.note: upset means turned over, and in a down clue that flips the letters to read upwards

blocks.note: AM is ante meridiem, before noon
a bit is a spell or stint of time
no plus I, the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Wishing nobody would be upset by the morning meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No-one' looks like nobody, but splits as NO + I before turning round. BIT for a session is loose, as in doing a bit or a stint.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambition is a hope or aspiration one works towards.

clue.text: Hair cutter's instrument holding shaver head is very clever

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: a razor cuts hair
first letter of shaver
the harp is a stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A barber's tool with a shaving head is extremely sharp.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is loose: the 'holding' only joins the head letter to the instrument, which follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: Razor-sharp describes a keen, quick mind as well as a keen blade.

clue.text: Steer clear of first lady's clothing commercial

indicators.note: clothing wraps round the body, so one word dresses another

blocks.note: Eve was the first woman in Genesis
an ad is a commercial

explanation.surface: Avoid the President's wife's outfit advertisement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First lady' wants to be the President's wife, but here she is the first woman of all: EV(AD)E.
explanation.definitionFit: To evade is to avoid or steer clear of something.

clue.text: Supporting a cause that's off the main track

blocks.note: first meaning: taking a side
second meaning: a short railway line beside the main line

explanation.surface: Backing a fringe campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: Siding is both taking someone's part and a railway branch line for parking trains.

clue.text: Small hawk is fearless

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
to hawk goods is to tout them

explanation.surface: A little bird of prey shows no fear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hawk' wants to be a bird; it is the verb meaning sell.
explanation.definitionFit: Stout can mean brave and resolute, as in stout-hearted.

clue.text: Briefly visible by the camera, run inside

indicators.note: inside says the runner's letter goes within the phrase meaning caught on camera

blocks.note: in shot means within the camera's frame
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A quick glimpse of someone dashing into the camera's view.
explanation.walkthrough: IN SHOT takes R between its H and O: IN SH(R)OT.
explanation.definitionFit: 'In short' is an idiom meaning to put it concisely, the same as briefly.

clue.text: Aldrin's way beyond top grade flier

indicators.note: beyond sends the way word further along, after the top grade piece

blocks.note: Buzz Aldrin, the second man on the Moon
A is the highest exam grade
RD is the abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: An astronaut whose flying is better than first-rate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beyond' puts the way after the top grade, so the abbreviation for road closes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A buzzard is a bird of prey, and any bird is a flier.

clue.text: Change vote on condition

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing on another comes after it, so the vote is placed last

blocks.note: flu is an illness, a medical condition
a voter marks a cross on the ballot

explanation.surface: A conditional vote for reform.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'A on B' means A follows B, so the cross comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: Flux is a state of continual change or instability.

clue.text: Initially, Bill and Ben sound enthralled with each new vegetable

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the two names that follow
to be enthralled is to be held captive, so one piece sits held between two others

blocks.note: first letter of Bill
to utter is to make a sound
first letter of Ben
EA is the abbreviation for each
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: The children's TV Flowerpot Men, Bill and Ben, are delighted by every fresh vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill and Ben were the Flowerpot Men of a classic British children's TV show. Their two initials hold the word for sound between them, then the abbreviations for each and new follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A butter bean is a large pale lima bean, eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Go back to the drawing board, being drastic's a benefit

definitions.text: Go back to the drawing board

indicators.note: a drastic change is radical, so the letters before it are overhauled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
a gain is a benefit

explanation.surface: Starting from scratch can help, if you're willing to be radical.
explanation.definitionFit: Going back to the drawing board is an idiom for starting a plan over from the beginning.

clue.text: Miss the old retired minion

indicators.note: retired suggests withdrawing backwards, so the archaic word is read from the end

blocks.note: to miss something is to lack it
ye is the old form of the, as in Ye Olde Shoppe

explanation.surface: A young woman complains of an elderly pensioner's servant.
explanation.definitionFit: A lackey is a servile follower, just as a minion is a subservient underling.

clue.text: Desperado who the admirers concealed

indicators.note: concealed says the letters lie unseen within the words before it

blocks.note: the run of letters across these three words

explanation.surface: An outlaw kept secret by his fans.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from wHO THE ADmirers.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperado is a reckless person, and a hothead acts rashly without thinking.

clue.text: Face fluent, detailed analysis of wealth

indicators.note: read as de-tailed, it means the word before has lost its last letter
analysis breaks something into parts, so the letters are taken apart and rebuilt

blocks.note: taken as written
fluent without its tail

explanation.surface: A confident, thorough report on riches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' reads as thorough, but split as de-tailed it removes a final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Affluence is the state of having plenty of money, so it is a synonym of wealth.

clue.text: Censure study with little weight

blocks.note: a den is a private room for work or study
an ounce is a small unit of weight; with joins it on

explanation.surface: Criticise research that carries little importance.
explanation.definitionFit: To denounce is to condemn publicly, a stronger form of censure.

clue.text: Rash and spots fellow scratched beginning to sting

indicators.note: scratched means struck off, so a letter is removed from the word
beginning to picks out only the first letter of the following word

blocks.note: freckles are small brown spots on the skin
F is the abbreviation for fellow, the letter struck off
first letter of sting

explanation.surface: A rash and spots, with a man scratching at the start of a sting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rash' looks like a skin complaint beside the spots and sting, but it is the adjective meaning impetuous.
explanation.definitionFit: Reckless and rash both describe acting without thought for consequences.

clue.text: Hoped church tower's protected in modern times

indicators.note: something protected in another is surrounded and guarded by it

blocks.note: AD, anno Domini, marks the current era
a spire is the tapering top of a church tower

explanation.surface: A church tower has been listed as a protected building in recent years.
explanation.walkthrough: AD, the era abbreviation, is the protector wrapped round the steeple. The 's stands for 'is' and joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To aspire is to hope for or aim at something, so aspired is past-tense hoped.

clue.text: Wife finally pursuing flirt, hurled pudding

indicators.note: hurled means thrown, so these letters are scattered into another order
finally picks out just the closing letter of the word beside it

blocks.note: taken as written
last letter of wife

explanation.surface: A wife, catching her husband with a flirt at last, throws a pudding at them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pursuing' puts the wife's last letter after the shuffled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A trifle is a British layered pudding of sponge, fruit, custard and cream.

clue.text: Shake bag containing arrows

blocks.note: first meaning: to tremble
second meaning: an archer's case for arrows

explanation.walkthrough: 'Containing' looks like an insertion signal but is part of the second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Quiver is both a verb for trembling and a noun for the case an archer carries arrows in.

clue.text: Knock half of pensioners travelling

indicators.note: half of keeps just the first five of the ten letters
travelling letters are on the move, ending in a new order

blocks.note: the first half of the word

explanation.surface: Criticism of half the pensioners on a coach trip.
explanation.definitionFit: To snipe is to make sly critical attacks, and to knock is to criticise.

clue.text: Not completely finished, baked potato's consumed at home

indicators.note: baking transforms something, so these letters are cooked into a new order
the word before it has swallowed the phrase for being indoors

blocks.note: time is up when it is finished
taken as written; the 's is 'has'
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: A half-eaten jacket potato left on the plate at home.
explanation.walkthrough: The scrambled potato letters, TOAPOT, take IN before their last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Up to a point' is an idiom meaning partly, to a limited extent.

clue.text: Rings up boozer filled with students

indicators.note: something filled with another holds it inside
in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top

blocks.note: a sot is a drunkard
L is a learner driver, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A pub full of students calls round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boozer' wants to be the British word for a pub; here it is the drinker.
explanation.definitionFit: A bell tolls when it rings slowly and repeatedly.

clue.text: Refuse unwanted emails

blocks.note: first meaning: rubbish, discarded stuff
second meaning: spam

explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' reads as a verb (say no to), but it is the noun meaning rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Junk is both worthless rubbish and the term for unsolicited mail and email.

clue.text: Be aware of denial in report

indicators.note: a report is something spoken, so the word is as it would be heard

blocks.note: no is a denial

explanation.surface: Knowing a refusal appears in the paperwork.
explanation.definitionFit: To know something is to be aware of it.

clue.text: Mediterranean-style house popular with bad guy

blocks.note: a villa is a holiday house of the Mediterranean type
something in is fashionable

explanation.surface: A seaside villa that's a favourite with movie gangsters.
explanation.definitionFit: A villain is the wrongdoer of a story, the bad guy.

clue.text: Atonement writer's great describing north

indicators.note: in crosswords to describe can mean to draw a line around, so one word encircles another

blocks.note: a pen is a writing instrument
ace means excellent
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: An author's fine account of the north, perhaps Ian McEwan's novel Atonement.
explanation.walkthrough: PEN, then ACE holding N: PEN + A(N)CE.
explanation.definitionFit: Penance is an act of self-punishment done to atone for wrongdoing.

clue.text: Took umbrage when entrees brought out with first of desserts

indicators.note: dishes brought out are rearranged on the table, so these letters move about
first of picks out only the opening letter of the next word

blocks.note: taken as written
first letter of desserts

explanation.surface: A diner got cross when the main courses arrived alongside the puddings.
explanation.definitionFit: To resent something is to take umbrage, or offence, at it.

clue.text: Confectionery assortments you and I tucked into

indicators.note: something tucked into another is pushed inside it

blocks.note: a set is a collection or assortment
we is you and I together

explanation.surface: The two of us digging into boxes of mixed chocolates.
explanation.walkthrough: SETS opens to take WE: S(WE)ETS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweets is the British word for candy, and confectionery is the collective name for them.
